content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Flow Transformations and Operators** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. Flow represents an asynchronous stream collected from a coroutine; flow operators, cancellation, buffering, and sharing determine behavior. Use the subtopics—Mapping and Filtering Flows, Buffering and Combining, Sequential and Concurrent Collection—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Flow represents an asynchronous stream collected from a coroutine; flow operators, cancellation, buffering, and sharing determine behavior.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it

items.title: Mapping and Filtering Flows
items.text: Mapping and Filtering Flows depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.

items.title: Buffering and Combining
items.text: Buffering and Combining should be evaluated against input size, allocation behavior, and workload. Start with a correctness test and reproducible measurement; choose the simplest implementation that meets the requirement.

items.title: Sequential and Concurrent Collection
items.text: Sequential and Concurrent Collection is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This example requires kotlinx-coroutines-core (and the matching Flow APIs where used). Run it in a Kotlin/JVM Gradle project; do not paste it into a plain browser preview.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A suspend function always runs on a background thread automatically.
